state: Project: JobRadar, a DataTalksClub AI Dev Tools Zoomcamp FINAL PROJECT by a solo student. Single user (the owner), no auth, no multi-tenancy. Feature: upload a resume; a watchlist of companies; a poller fetches each company's public Greenhouse job-board JSON (no API key needed); new postings pass a deterministic prefilter then one LLM call that returns a score 0-100 plus why-it-fits and gaps; a daily email digest lists new matches above a cutoff, and sends nothing when there is nothing new. A 'Run digest now' button in the UI can trigger it on demand. Stack: React frontend whose build is served as static files by a FastAPI backend in ONE Docker container, so there is one URL and no CORS. Storage is SQLAlchemy over SQLite locally and Postgres in production. The poller is an HTTP endpoint (POST /internal/tick with a shared secret), not a separate worker service. Grading is by peer reviewers who score a public rubric: README problem description, documented AI-assisted workflow incl. MCP, architecture, frontend with tests, OpenAPI contract, backend with tests, database supporting different environments, containerization, integration tests, DEPLOYMENT WITH A WORKING URL, CI/CD that tests and deploys, reproducibility. The reviewer will open the URL during a review window that may be weeks after submission. Constraints already verified: Render free web services spin down after 15 minutes idle and take about 1 minute to wake; Render free Postgres EXPIRES 30 DAYS after creation and is then deleted; GitHub Actions scheduled workflows drift by minutes to hours and can be skipped entirely, and schedules are disabled after 60 days of repository inactivity; Neon offers a durable free Postgres. The student has prior experience from coursework with Docker Compose, GitHub Actions, FastAPI, React, SQLite and Kubernetes/kind, and wants the least work that still scores well rather than the most impressive architecture.

questions.question: Which deployment target should this project use for the single container plus Postgres, optimizing for a reliably working public URL over the peer-review window and low setup effort?

options.render_plus_neon: Render free Docker web service for the app plus a Neon free Postgres instead of Render's 30-day-expiring database; accept the 15-minute spin-down and ~1 minute cold start on first visit
options.render_only: Render free Docker web service and accept Render's free Postgres that is deleted 30 days after creation
options.fly: Fly.io with a machine that auto-stops and their Postgres, more moving parts but no spin-down deletion surprise
options.cloudrun: Google Cloud Run plus a Cloud Run Job and Neon Postgres, scale-to-zero with a generous free tier but requires GCP billing and a larger CI/CD setup
options.railway: Railway, simple Git deploys but the free allowance is small and may run out during the review window

questions.question: Should the project repository be public or private or local-only, given that peer reviewers need to inspect the code and the README?

options.public_github: A public GitHub repository, so reviewers can open the code and the CI runs contribute to the grade with no access request
options.private_github: A private GitHub repository, default safety, but reviewers cannot see the code without being invited
options.local_only: Local git only, no GitHub at all, which removes CI/CD from the rubric coverage

questions.question: What should be the primary trigger for the daily digest, given that GitHub Actions cron is unreliable?

options.gh_actions_primary: Use the GitHub Actions scheduled workflow as the primary trigger and accept drift and occasional skipped runs
options.button_primary: Treat the in-app 'Run digest now' button as the reliable path and the scheduled workflow as a best-effort convenience, documenting the drift
options.external_cron: Use an external free cron service that pings the endpoint on a schedule

questions.question: Is turning the poller into an endpoint inside the single web container, rather than deploying a separate worker service, a sound choice for this project given the grading rubric and the reliability constraints described?

criteria.true: the single-container endpoint approach still satisfies the rubric and survives the described free-tier and cron behaviour
criteria.false: a separate worker service or an in-process scheduler is actually required for the project to work or score well
